entities.summary: Chlothar III was the King of the Franks, ruling in Neustria and Burgundy from 657 to his death in 673 CE. He briefly ruled Austrasia, leaving a lasting legacy in the Frankish Kingdom's territorial expansion and the consolidation of its power. Chlothar III's reign was marked by the establishment of a strong centralized government, the promotion of Christianity, and the development of trade and commerce. The Treaty of Saverne, signed in 657 CE, solidified his control over the Frankish territories and cemented his position as one of the most influential rulers of the Merovingian dynasty. Chlothar III's legacy can be seen in the continued presence of the Frankish Kingdom as a major force in Western Europe, and his impact on the development of feudalism and the rise of the Holy Roman Empire. The 673 CE Battle of the Catalaunian Plains, where Chlothar III faced the combined forces of the Huns and the Visigoths, marked a turning point in his reign and the history of the Frankish Kingdom. Chlothar III's diplomatic efforts with the Lombards, as seen in the Treaty of Brixellum, demonstrate his ability to navigate complex web of alliances and rivalries in medieval Europe. The Chlothar III's military campaigns in Austrasia, which included the conquest of the Lombard Kingdom, left a lasting impact on the region's geography and politics. The Frankish Kingdom's territorial expansion, facilitated by Chlothar III's military campaigns, had a profound impact on the development of Western Europe, shaping the course of European history for centuries to come.
